parsed.summary: The Lean theorem states that for n ≥ 3, k ≥ 1, R > 0 and positive r_1..r_k, the following are equivalent. (1) There exist open neighborhoods U_i of the closed capacity-r_i balls in ℂ^n, with smooth topological embeddings f_i : U_i → ℂ^n that preserve the standard symplectic form, sending each closed ball into the open capacity-R ball, with pairwise disjoint images of the closed balls. (2) Σ r_i^n < R^n and r_i + r_j < R for i ≠ j. This matches Theorem 1.1 of the paper. No substantive caveat was found. The only nuance is that the neighborhood U_i is not itself required to map into the target, which is harmless because the neighborhood can be shrunk.

glossary.note: Real subtraction; the sign convention is irrelevant for preservation.

glossary.plain: U is open, f is C^∞ on U, f|_U is a topological embedding, and Df(x) preserves ω0 for every x ∈ U
glossary.standard_concept: symplectic embedding defined on open U
glossary.note: Df(x) is symplectic linear, hence injective, so f is an immersion. An immersion that is a topological embedding is a smooth embedding. fderiv is genuine since f is smooth on open U.

glossary.plain: There exist open U_i ⊇ B(r_i) and symplectic embeddings f_i on U_i with f_i(B(r_i)) ⊆ int B(R), and f_i(B(r_i)) disjoint from f_j(B(r_j)) for i ≠ j
glossary.note: Only the closed ball, not U_i, must map into the target. This is equivalent, since U_i can be shrunk by compactness.

glossary.plain: Σ r_i^n < R^n and r_i + r_j < R for i ≠ j

lean_claims.plain: For naturals n ≥ 3, k ≥ 1, real R > 0, and r : Fin k → ℝ with all r_i > 0: HasPacking n k R r ↔ (Σ r_i^n < R^n ∧ ∀ i ≠ j, r_i + r_j < R).

paper_claims.plain: For n ≥ 3, k ≥ 1 and positive R, R_1..R_k, there is a symplectic embedding ⊔ B^{2n}(R_i) ↪ int B^{2n}(R) iff Σ R_i^n < R^n and R_i + R_j < R for i < j. Here embeddings of closed balls are defined on open neighborhoods and have pairwise disjoint compact images.

coverage.why: Same dimension and count hypotheses, the same capacity convention, closed source and open target, embeddings on neighborhoods, disjoint images, and the same inequalities.

flags.explanation: The neighborhood U_i is not required to map into int B(R); only the closed ball is. The paper's notion presumably has the whole embedding land in the target. These are equivalent, since f_i^{-1}(int B(R)) ∩ U_i is an open neighborhood of the compact ball. So this is not a mismatch, just a presentational difference.
flags.probe_idea: Prove that HasPacking implies the variant requiring Set.MapsTo (f i) (U i) (openBall n R), by shrinking U i to U i ∩ f i ⁻¹' openBall n R.

flags.explanation: The embedding is required to be topological, plus smooth with symplectic derivative, rather than a smooth embedding stated directly. This is equivalent because a symplectic linear map is injective.
flags.probe_idea: Show that ∀ x ∈ U, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ f x) follows from the form-preservation clause, using the nondegeneracy of standardForm.

lint_verdicts.why: The subtraction is in ℝ (products of real and imaginary parts), not ℕ.
x ranges over the open set U on which f is C^∞, so f is differentiable at x and fderiv is the true derivative.
